newsitem.title: USA: GMAC global floater tops U.S. new corp bond issues.
newsitem.headline: GMAC global floater tops U.S. new corp bond issues.

text.p: General Motor Acceptance Corp's (GMAC) $750 million global offering of floating-rate notes is expected to be the largest deal to hit a generally sluggish U.S. corporate bond new issue market on Wendesday, market players said.
GMAC, the finance subsidiary of General Motors Corp, may increase the size of the offering of five-year floaters to $1 billion if demand is strong, they said.
Price talk on the deal is currently 18 basis points to 20 basis points over three-month Libor, they said.
A syndicate official away from the GMAC deal said, "A floater versus a fixed-rate structure is typical of a bearish market--this to some degree speaks to where market sentiment is currently."
But another syndicate official downplayed the significance of GMAC's use of a floating-rate structure, saying GMAC has issued floaters under a variety of market conditions in the past.
The GMAC offering is expected to be priced later on Wednesday via joint-lead-managers Morgan Stanley & Co and UBS Securities, market sources said.
National Westminster Bank PLC is also expected to offer $500 million in step-up perpetual notes via J.P. Morgan Securities later on Wednesday.
The offering is the U.K. bank's first yankee since 1993 and its first ever step-up perpetual issue in the U.S.
A market source said, "This paper is attractive to investors becuase they can buy paper rated AA3/A-plus that still has some spread."
The coupon on the notes pays at a fixed-rate for 10.5 years and then steps up by 100 basis points into a Libor-floater.
